recorded.outcome:q-named-check: Settled. Reference table row 'record | generated from its components: `Bulk[percent=12]` | a `Map` you write | constructor arguments' shows a record prints its type name and its parameter, and takes per-use parameters as constructor arguments. Section: 'a 12 % bulk rate for one tenant and 8 % for another needs a class or a lambda that captures the rate'; 'a lambda or a small record for policies built from configuration'. Together these confirm the option's claim that each instance prints its own type and threshold.

recorded.prompt:q-deadline-sort: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-deadline-sort: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-deadline-sort: Summary: 'A comparator that subtracts overflows, and List.sort returns a wrong order or throws, depending on the input'; section: 'Which of the two you get depends on the input, so one customer's history page throws and another's is silently misordered' and 'whether the sort ever asks about that pair depends on the input order'. The reader has to work out that minutes in nanoseconds exceed an int, using 'yes, when the difference doesn't fit an int' (reference table) and the 30-day ms example. Minor caveat: the 3-element example shows one input order ([A-3, A-2, A-1]) that sorts correctly, so 'out of order' isn't guaranteed for every input. With many jobs spread over minutes, the page's 1,000-order runs support the option.

recorded.prompt:q-named-check:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-named-check:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-named-check:a: Refuted: 'A constant can't take parameters per use, so a 12 % bulk rate for one tenant and 8 % for another needs a class or a lambda that captures the rate. And each constant is a single object per class loader'; reference table: 'none: one instance per constant'.
recorded.prompt:q-named-check:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-named-check:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-named-check:c: Refuted: 'The lambda's toString() is a generated class name that can change between runs'. The example assigns the lambda to a named variable (bulkLambda) and it still prints 'Pricing$$Lambda/0x00007126dc000c08@330bedb4'. The example uses a local variable, not a static final field, but the passage is general.
recorded.prompt:q-named-check:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-named-check:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-named-check:d: Refuted by the example: PricingPolicy is annotated @FunctionalInterface, yet the lambda prints 'Pricing$$Lambda/...', named after the enclosing class, not the interface. The page does not state the annotation's actual purpose (the 'says' text), but the option's claim is contradicted.

recorded.pass:q-shared-builder:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shared-builder:a: Refuted: '`volatile` made it far worse ... it doesn't make `+=` atomic' (1,521,082 wrong vs 10,078); summary: '`volatile` makes the race more frequent'. The page's case is primitive fields, not a reference to a mutable builder, but the claim that volatile fixes a shared field is refuted.
